precepts.text: Mattathias had five sons, Joannan and Jonathan among them, John and John; the same name in one family was common in Israel.
precepts.point: Israel named sons the same name: Mattathias had Joannan and Jonathan, there were three Marys at the cross and Simons everywhere, so two Zerubbabels is no puzzle.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Matthew names Christ's family: “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” Mary his mother and Mary his aunt at the cross, a brother named Simon among Simons everywhere: Israel used the same names over and over, even inside one family. The Maccabees prove it.

“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest.” “And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: Simon; called Thassi: Judas, who was called Maccabeus: Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus.” Stop at Jonathan. Joannan and Jonathan are the same name: John and John, two sons of one father. Like George Foreman naming his sons George, George, George and George.

So it was a common thing for Israel to name sons the same name. You had Mary and Mary, John and John, John the Baptist too; they loved that name. You had Simon Iscariot, Simon the Canaanite, Simon Peter, and Christ's own brother Simon. That is why two Zerubbabels in the genealogies is no puzzle at all.

precepts.point: Israel named sons the same name: Mattathias had Joannan and Jonathan, there were three Marys at the cross and Simons everywhere, so two Zerubbabels is no puzzle.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
In Matthew his own people asked, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” John shows his own disciples said the same thing: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

The son of who? The son of Joseph. The one Moses and the prophets wrote about is called by his disciple the son of Joseph, the carpenter.

And Matthew says he had brethren, James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and sisters, more than one: a bunch of siblings. James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. So you Christians who say Mary was a virgin who never had sex read this all the time. Now some hear us teach it and act like they came up with it, saying the Roman Catholic doctrine is wrong, playing catchup. Christ had a father and a mother, brothers and sisters.

precepts.text: In his own synagogue they said, is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James and Joses and Juda and Simon, and are not his sisters here with us? They knew his family and were offended at him.
precepts.point: Israel named sons the same name: Mattathias had Joannan and Jonathan, there were three Marys at the cross and Simons everywhere, so two Zerubbabels is no puzzle.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account as Matthew 13. On the sabbath Christ “began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things?” Then: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.”

They knew his family. They knew his background, his mother, his brothers by name, and his sisters. Who do he think he is? We grew up with this guy. He ain't nobody special. You're from the hood like us, from Nazareth; what you talking about, Savior? In his own home, where he was from, he got disrespected by his own neighbors and family members.

So the scripture itself shows Christ was born into a real family, the son of Mary with brothers and sisters, and that the people offended at him were the ones who knew exactly where he came from.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Isaiah 9:7 says, “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Why does it say the increase of his government? Christ answers in a parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.”

A mustard seed is one of the smallest of all seeds, and that is how the kingdom of heaven is on the earth now. “but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.” When it is grown is the increase. All nations are going to submit to it and follow what it says.

We are at that mustard seed stage now. A lot of people say that Israelite thing ain’t nothing. Oh no, it is something: it is the beginning of God’s government. And it is only going to increase. When you check the history from the time of Nat Turner, you might think it ended there. It did not. Look at the history of the Israelite schools; we here are part of that great history, part of that mustard seed that, when it is grown, is the greatest of all. You are not tricking us back into worshipping white Jesus.

So the throne of Isaiah 16:5, established in mercy in the tabernacle of David, starts small and grows until every nation lodges under it.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
In the parable, “while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat”. A mixing happened: bad seed sown in among the good seed. “An enemy hath done this.” It was done on purpose. For the Northern Kingdom tribes in this hemisphere, that was the whitening the Spaniards practiced: marrying to lighter skin to better the race, with a whole caste system of names for every kind of mixing. They found the tribes, and since they could not kill us all outright, they tried to pollute the royal seed. But however watered down the daughter is, one man with the seed of an Israelite brings it back.

The servants asked, should we gather up the tares? “Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest”. It is not for us to determine, because of the way this went down; we do not know who is and who is not. At the harvest the angels will know who is Israel.

Amos proves it: “For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Why among all nations? Because through the whitening, the mixing and the captivities, God himself has to be the one to sift us. “Like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” It will be determined who is who. Even Adam had to walk through a gate; you do not have twelve gates with twelve names and think somebody is going to sneak through. God said he will do it. My sheep hear my voice, and you know them by their works.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” He is going to kill a lot of them, before, during and even some after. So we narrow down where our people gather and go to the chief places of concourse, not to where the Edomites are, and give the word; and let God do the separating.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Christ said: “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given to the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; it is not given to everyone. Once these men understand it, God having revealed it to them, they reveal it to the people and the people understand it. It is given to the apostles first and foremost.

That is the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom. There is hidden wisdom even about Adam: did Adam have a kingdom? People think he was running around butt naked. No; it is hidden wisdom.

“but to them it is not given”. That is why there is no need to argue with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving. If God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it. As Paul says, “the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why try to force him to know it? Correct them and dust off your shoes, because everyone is not going to get the things of the Spirit of God.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” The mysteries are given to some and not to others. “For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.”

Christ told Nicodemus how that works: “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” The wind goes where it will, and you cannot say where it comes from or where it goes; so is every one born of the Spirit. The word rests on those it is given to. That is why it is given to the disciples to know the mysteries and not to the others, and why the one who has receives more while the one who has not loses even what he has.

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed, but understand not; make the heart of this people fat, lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: They saw the works and did not perceive. The heart was made fat and the ears heavy so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”. Here is that prophecy as it was given to Isaiah: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

They saw the works and did not perceive. Isaiah was told to make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, lest they convert and be healed. It was done to them on purpose, so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come. Matthew says the same: their heart is waxed gross, their ears are dull of hearing, their eyes they have closed, “lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.” That is why he spoke to them in parables, and why the ones who heard him and saw his works did not understand.

precepts.text: Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
precepts.point: The good ground hears and understands, and brings others in behind him.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.”

Mark names the wicked one and tells how fast he moves: “And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.” The wicked one is Satan, and he comes immediately. The man on the way side hears the word and does not understand it, and before it can take hold Satan has taken it away.

That is the first of the four grounds. The stony ground receives it with joy and has no root, and is offended when tribulation or persecution arises, which can come through family or through a job. The thorns are the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, which choke the word. The good ground hears and understands, bears fruit, and brings others in behind him. On the way side the word never gets that far; Satan takes it the moment it is heard.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree”. This work starts small and ends covering the earth.

Moses said how the doctrine goes out: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”. Rain and dew do not fall on one spot; they come down over everything. The doctrine goes out over the whole earth because Israel is scattered over the whole earth, and the small rain has to reach the tender herb wherever it is. So the least of all seeds becomes the greatest among herbs: the doctrine that starts small comes down like the showers upon the grass until it has covered the earth where Israel is.

precepts.why:
“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High”: that’s what most people miss. When I came in the truth in 1990, what we wanted to hear was prophecies; we wanted to hear the white man is the devil and the intricacies of the scriptures. But when it came to the law, the law classes were empty. Teach the prophecies and the crowd would come around; teach the law and you see everybody leave. Nobody wanted to hear that.

“And is occupied in the meditation thereof”, of God’s law, “will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” See it as a step to understanding the prophecies, and to get the better understanding. That’s why the first thing is the law of the Most High, followed by seeking out the wisdom of all the ancient, and being occupied in prophecies. That’s the order of understanding.

That’s what a lot of Israelites miss, and this is why you hear strange doctrines out there about raping women, about polygyny, having a group of women. But you won’t find one scripture from the time of the Assyrian captivity on of Israel in captivity in another land having a group of women as their wives. You won’t read it in the Bible. You working in McDonald’s, you working in Home Depot with a group of women, and the women is the one making the money, taking care of his rusty black behind? Selling oils on the oil table? You’ve got to be kidding me. And if you fell for that, shame on you. Don’t come running over here, being wife number three, talking about now I want to get my life right. We’ve been warning for years; you saw us on the street teaching and you gave us the finger. Now he kicked you to the curb and got another wife number three, and you mad now. Well, shame on you, sister.

“He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also.” Why? Because he learned God’s law. He understood the law, and now he says, now I’m ready to get into these parables; now I can understand, because I understand the law.

“He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.” That’s why, when I get around the Bishops, the deacons and the captains, that’s what we talk about: the grave sentences and dark parables. That’s why it says how beautiful it is for brethren to dwell together in unity, and iron sharpeneth iron.
